channel.title: NewsCenter — Top 5 news of the day — 2026-11-24
channel.description: The five news that matter most today, chosen from Laurent's newsletters. 104 news received.

item.title: 1. Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after initially rejecting his return
item.description: Why it matters: Nvidia’s reinstatement of Jensen Huang after an investigation creates immediate leadership, governance and market implications for the most strategically important AI-chip company. Nvidia’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as chairman, chief executive officer, and director five days after rejecting his return. The independent investigation continues, while Nvidia shares rebounded sharply after the announcement.

item.title: 2. CrowdStrike acquires Zscaler in the largest cybersecurity deal
item.description: Why it matters: CrowdStrike’s all-stock acquisition of Zscaler would create a major end-to-end cybersecurity platform and reshape competition in enterprise security. CrowdStrike will acquire Zscaler in an all-stock transaction. The combined company will cover enterprise security from devices to the cloud.

item.title: 3. Virginia and Oregon sue Elon Musk’s companies
item.description: Why it matters: Virginia and Oregon’s lawsuits against Elon Musk’s companies could bring significant legal, regulatory and reputational consequences for AI safety and platform governance. Virginia and Oregon have sued Elon Musk’s companies, alleging that Grok lacked adequate safeguards against child sexual abuse material and non-consensual intimate images. These are allegations, not judicial findings.

item.title: 4. The EU Chips Act Unlocks €33 Billion in Investment
item.description: Why it matters: The EU Chips Act’s €33 billion investment package signals a major effort to strengthen Europe’s semiconductor capacity and reduce supply-chain dependence. Europe has unlocked €33 billion to revive its semiconductor industry, with new factories, GaN power-production sites, and packaging and testing lines spread across more than 20 projects. However, commercial production will not begin immediately.

item.title: 5. OpenAI deploys GPT-6.2 Sol in ChatGPT’s Chat tab
item.description: Why it matters: OpenAI’s lower-cost GPT-6.2 Sol deployment could materially change the economics of everyday AI use across ChatGPT, enterprise products and APIs. OpenAI is adding a chat-optimized version of GPT-6.2 Sol to ChatGPT’s Chat tab. Sol and Astra are also available in ChatGPT Work, Codex, and the API; OpenAI says Sol delivers performance close to Astra’s at about one-fifth the cost.
